guide_bridge_td_auth: When sub-Claude hits an MCP elicitation (an "Allow access?" dialog), its TTY is blocked by the modal and can't answer itself. Main dispatches key codes (124/125/36/36 = right / left / Enter / Enter) via osascript to pick "Allow all" on sub's behalf.
guide_bridge_td_terminal: Main Claude pushes commands into another Terminal.app window via osascript do script in window id, and reads output back with get contents of selected tab. No broker, no focus theft.

guide_cc_channel_p_automation: The bridge has six built-in automation mechanisms that keep the Claude Code channel running unattended. All of them can be toggled via environment variables.
guide_cc_channel_p_autowake: Claude Code is a reactive agent — after /clear or on a new session, incoming MCP notifications don't automatically start a turn. After forwarding a message, the bridge waits ECLAW_AUTO_WAKE_DELAY_S seconds (default 10) then inspects tmux state; if idle, it injects a “process pending channel messages” string via tmux send-keys to trigger a new turn. A cooldown of ECLAW_AUTO_WAKE_COOLDOWN_S seconds prevents spam.
guide_cc_channel_p_cmd_auto_approve: Toggle auto-approve mode. When ON, the bridge's /ask endpoint auto-returns approve for every PreToolUse hook request and stops pushing approval rich cards — useful for leaving Claude running long automated tasks. Send the command again to toggle OFF.
guide_cc_channel_p_cmd_model: Switch the model Claude Code uses. The bridge replies with a rich card letting you pick ⚡ Sonnet / 🧠 Opus / 🪶 Haiku; after your choice, the bridge auto-restarts the Claude Code session to load the new model.

guide_cc_channel_p_context: The bridge reads the tmux pane every 60 seconds to detect Claude Code's N% until auto-compact indicator. At 20% remaining it sends a warning; at 5% it auto-runs /clear to free context. This prevents Claude from behaving erratically (e.g. giving up on MCP tools and falling back to Playwright browser automation) when context is nearly exhausted. Disable with ECLAW_CONTEXT_WATCH_ENABLED=false.
guide_cc_channel_p_enforcer: The bridge tracks whether each user message gets answered via the reply tool. If ECLAW_REPLY_TIMEOUT_S seconds (default 120) pass without a reply while Claude is still busy (e.g. a browser session is open), the bridge auto-injects a reminder: “Don't use Playwright to click the UI — use the reply tool”, nudging Claude back to the correct reply path.
guide_cc_channel_p_envvars: Full list of bridge environment variables. Required ones are marked ✅; the rest are optional and fall back to the listed defaults.
guide_cc_channel_p_errorloop: When the bridge fails to deliver a reply to the EClaw API (expired API Key, network error, quota exceeded, etc.), notifyClaudeError injects the error into Claude's channel inbox so Claude knows the previous reply did not reach the user and can retry or adjust. The user also sees a bridge error hint on the next message.
guide_cc_channel_p_faq_context: A classic symptom of context pressure — Claude “forgets” the fakechat instructions. The Context Pressure Monitor (20% warning / 5% auto /clear) and Reply Tool Enforcer should handle this automatically. You can also manually send Escape + /clear in the tmux pane to reset context immediately.

guide_cc_channel_p_faq_log: The bridge log is at /tmp/eclaw-bridge.log; the PreToolUse hook log is at /tmp/eclaw-hook.log.
guide_cc_channel_p_faq_reply_fail: Usual causes: expired ECLAW_API_KEY, claude.ai weekly quota exhausted, or a transient 5xx from the EClaw API. The Error Feedback Loop pushes the error into Claude's inbox and the user also sees a bridge hint. Rotate the API key or wait for the quota reset to recover.
guide_cc_channel_p_kanban_queue: By default the bridge treats automated messages from EClaw's kanban board as Claude's work queue and forwards them (ECLAW_FORWARD_KANBAN=true). If the bot hits a context overflow and you need emergency mute, temporarily set it to false to stop forwarding kanban messages without affecting user-initiated messages.
